title: E155 Portfolio
text:
Natalie Ko is an Engineering Major at Harvey Mudd College with a Science, Technology, and Society concentration. She’s interested in mechatronics and robotics. On campus, she works as a Repair Steward for Harvey Mudd’s Makerspace, CAD Lab TA/Grutor/Designer for the E4 course, and Shop Proctor for the Machine Shop.
When Natalie isn’t working on coursework or on-campus jobs, she works on other cool Engineering personal projects, including iterating on functional Spiderman web-shooters since 2018. She’s primarily drawn to projects that help foster a more accessible world.

title: Lab 1 Report: FPGA and MCU Setup and Testing
text: In this lab, the E155 development board was assembled and tested to confirm the NUCLEO-32 MCU and UPduino v3.1 FPGA functionality. A design was implemented on the FPGA to control an on-board LED with the on-board high-speed oscillator, as well as control two additional on-board LEDs and an external 7-segment display using combinational logic of four switch inputs.

title: Lab 1 Report: FPGA and MCU Setup and Testing
text:
Design and Testing Methodology
To design the LED and 7-segment display implementation, modules etc.
The design was first tested using waveform simulation in QuestaSim
Then, several testbenches were written and run to confirm the outputs of each sub-module and the top-level module in each possible input case.
Finally, the 7-segment display circuit was built and connected to the FPGA GPIO pins, and the full design was uploaded to the FPGA and deployed on the hardware. The design was tested by toggling the switches to account for all cases and observing the LED and 7-segment display outputs ton confirm functionality.
